title: Why look beyond positive and negative reviews?
text: Why look beyond positive and negative reviews?
Perfume reviews describe sensory impressions and emotional associations.
Two positive reviews; different emotional meanings. Illustrative examples.

title: One review can express several emotions
text: One review can express several emotions
“This perfume makes me happy, and I cannot wait to wear it.”
The task allows multiple emotion labels for the same perfume, based on its review text.
Target: emotion expressed in review language. Wearer responses are not directly measured.

title: Three research questions
text: How can perfume-review transcripts be represented as structured emotion features?
How do machine learning and deep learning methods compare in identifying multiple emotions?
How does weighted augmentation with generated reviews affect prediction on held-out YouTube perfumes?

title: What this thesis contributes
text: English YouTube transcript records linked to 784 perfumes.
A 58-feature representation alongside a direct text modelling route.
Five models, feature combinations and weighted synthetic augmentation.
Shared evaluation conditions connect the dataset, representations and experiments.

title: The evidence does not establish a general augmentation benefit
source: Thesis §4.4.3; Table 11. Paired source-group bootstrap intervals.
text: The evidence does not establish a general augmentation benefit
Thesis §4.4.3; Table 11. Paired source-group bootstrap intervals.
The direction and size of changes differ across models and metrics.
Under equal source-group weighting, all five 95% intervals for seven-label Macro AP change include zero.
This experiment does not isolate why the models respond differently.
Generated text needs validation on natural reviews before it can be assumed beneficial.

title: Answers to the research questions
text: 58 features combine word counts, affect dimensions and contextual scores. Their effects depend on the classifier.
BERT leads pooled F1 and AP; XGBoost leads ROC-AUC. The evidence does not establish an overall best model.
Weighted augmentation produces model- and metric-dependent changes, without a consistent general benefit.

title: The scope of the conclusions
text:
Grouping addresses shared videos and identical transcripts.
Dependence through reviewers or channels may remain.
Conclusions apply to this dataset, annotation policy and experimental configuration.
tables: Agreement with human judgments is not established
Findings are specific to this review setting
Independence and estimation precision are limited

title: Three priorities for extending the work
text: Three priorities for extending the work

Check excerpt relevance.

Collect independent human annotations.

Add independent sources and rare-emotion cases.

Test new channels and platforms.

Use comparable review or perfume units.

Test generation strategies on independent natural reviews.

title: Three takeaways
text: Review transcripts become lexical, dimensional and contextual emotion features.
Five approaches show strengths that vary across metrics and emotions.
Generated reviews produce model-dependent changes, without consistent improvement.
A traceable dataset, a reproducible workflow and controlled evidence.
